updates.label: Midday
updates.title: Tech gives back gains; consumer confidence jumps
updates.summary: Chip stocks are pulling the Nasdaq lower after Monday's Nvidia-led surge, while the Dow is holding up. Consumer confidence jumped to its highest in nearly two years and discount and grocery retailers are rallying, with the 10-year steady near 4.92%.
key_points: Mid-morning: Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) about -2%, S&P 500 (SPY) about -0.7%, Dow (DIA) slightly up; Nvidia down ~5% after Monday's 31% jump
Conference Board consumer confidence rose to 103.3 in November from 91.9, well above the ~92 forecast and the highest since January 2025
Dollar Tree up ~11% on a Q3 beat: comps +4.6% with traffic +3.8%, full-year EPS guidance raised to $8.05-8.25; Best Buy up ~5% on +6.1% comps
Retail tenants and REITs firm: Target +4%, Dollar General +4%, Kroger +3%; Realty Income +1.1%, other retail REITs +0.3-0.8%; office REITs mixed
10-year Treasury ~4.92%, little changed; markets still price a December Fed hike at ~95%
updates.talking_point: Consumer confidence just hit a two-year high and discount retailers are reporting more foot traffic, so value and necessity tenants look like strong credit for retail space right now.

updates.label: After close
updates.title: Best day since April 2025; short-term yields rise
updates.summary: Stocks held their huge gains into the close on Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang, with the Nasdaq up about 6.5% and the S&P 500 near 4.7%, the best day since April 2025. Treasuries sold off as risk appetite returned, led by the 2-year, while the 10-year stayed near 4.94% and REITs gained only modestly.
key_points: Close: S&P 500 about +4.7%, Dow up roughly 1,450 points (~+3%), Nasdaq about +6.5%; Nvidia +31%
Treasuries fell, led by short maturities; traders dropped bets on a half-point December hike, but a quarter-point hike is still priced as likely
Late-day watchlist: VNQ +1.3%, SL Green +4%, Cushman +5%, CBRE/JLL +2-2.6%; Regency flat, Kroger -1.6%
Local: Times Free Press reports Weigel's planned Ringgold store may be its first outside Tennessee
Ahead: PCE inflation Wednesday, markets closed Thursday, 1 PM close Friday
updates.talking_point: Stocks just had their best day in 19 months, but the bond market barely moved: the 10-year is still near 4.9%, so it still sets cap rates and loan terms on retail deals.

updates.label: Midday
updates.title: Stocks rebound sharply as Nvidia reinstates Huang
updates.summary: Stocks are bouncing back hard from Friday's correction after Nvidia's board brought Jensen Huang back as CEO, with the Nasdaq up nearly 7% late morning. The 10-year is little changed near 4.94%, and REITs are lagging the rally.
key_points: Late morning: S&P 500 about +4.9% (~7,250), Dow +3.2% (~49,690), Nasdaq +6.7% (~24,135); VIX down to ~27
Nvidia up ~30% after its board reinstated Huang, who stepped down Nov 12; its internal investigation continues
10-year Treasury ~4.94%, up about 2 bp; markets still price a Dec 9 Fed hike near 90%
REITs trail: VNQ ~+1%, Simon +1%, Kimco and Realty Income under +0.5%, Regency and Federal slightly down; CBRE, JLL, Cushman up 2-4%
Short week: PCE inflation Wednesday, markets closed Thursday, early close Friday
updates.talking_point: Stocks bounced but rates didn't fall with them: the 10-year is holding near 4.9%, so pricing on retail deals is still set by the bond market, not the stock rebound.

updates.label: After close
updates.title: S&P 500 and Dow close in correction
updates.summary: The AI selloff picked up into the close: the S&P 500 fell 3.7% and the Nasdaq 5.3%, capping the worst week since April 2025 and putting the S&P 500 and Dow more than 10% below their records. Money kept moving into Treasuries, pulling the 10-year down to about 4.93%.
key_points: Week: S&P 500 about -8.6%, Dow -8.0%, Nasdaq -10.0%; S&P down seven straight days
Chips led the drop: Nvidia -13.8%, Micron -13.9%, AMD -13.3%; most stocks outside tech rose
10-year Treasury closed near 4.93%, down about 11 bp from 5.04% Thursday
Fed Gov. Cook said rates aren't high enough to beat inflation; a December hike is still priced as near-certain
updates.talking_point: The stock selloff is pulling the 10-year back under 5%, which takes some pressure off financing for well-leased retail even while the Fed signals a December hike.

updates.label: Midday
updates.title: AI selloff deepens; yields and REITs catch a bid
updates.summary: Tech is leading a second straight down day as AI-spending doubts spread after Anthropic's IPO, but money is rotating into Treasuries and rate-sensitive real estate. The 10-year has slipped back to about 5.0% from Monday's 5%+ levels.
key_points: Late morning: Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) about -3%, S&P 500 (SPY) about -1.5%, Dow (DIA) roughly flat; VIX near 31, highest since March
Chips hit hardest: Nvidia ~-7%, Micron and AMD ~-10%+; Nasdaq 100 ~8% below last Friday's close
10-year Treasury ~4.99%, down ~6 bp today and off ~5.2% a week ago
Retail REITs up 1-1.6% (Realty Income, Kimco, Brixmor); office REITs BXP and SL Green up ~1.2%
Michigan consumer sentiment rose to 51.5 in November from 48.0
updates.talking_point: Even with stocks selling off, rates easing back toward 5% is helping real estate: net lease and grocery-anchored REITs are up today while tech falls.

monday.title: Market Brief — week of November 16, 2026
monday.summary: Rates are going up while retail space stays scarce: financing is harder, but the space itself is still in demand. The 10-year is back above 5% and futures price a December 9 Fed hike, while retail vacancy sits near record lows and office is stabilizing only at the top end.
key_points: 10-year Treasury back above 5% (5.17% intraday Fri); futures price a Dec 9 Fed hike at ~88% (forecast)
October CPI +0.4%, core +0.3% for a third straight month — inflation still sticky
Jobs beat: +165K payrolls, unemployment 4.1%
Retail is tight: national vacancy ~4.3–5.9%, record-low new supply, rents up ~2.5% y/y
Office: CBRE vacancy 18.2% and falling; sublease space lowest since 2020, but Class B/C still weak
Distress rising: CMBS special servicing 11.74%, highest since 2012; retail delinquency +63 bp in October
Local: $900M+ downtown construction; Hwy 153 Chick-fil-A traded at a 4.15% cap — the corridor's top-of-market comp
monday.talking_point: Good strip and pad space is the scarcest it's been in years — credit-tenant deals on 153 still trade tight even with the 10-year above 5%.

friday.title: What Moved — week of Nov 16, 2026
friday.summary: A rough week for stocks: the Dow was down about 6% through Thursday, its worst week since April 2025, as the AI trade faded even after Nvidia beat estimates. Rates stayed near 5% and the Fed looks set to hike December 8–9, while October shoppers kept spending.
key_points: Dow down ~6% through Thursday; all three indexes fell 2%+ on Thursday alone
Nvidia beat ($115.8B revenue vs ~$109B expected) but the stock slid; Anthropic IPO priced at $83, opened $111.50, ~$92 Friday
10-year ~4.99%; futures price a Dec 8–9 hike as nearly certain (~90% for 25bp, 10% for 50bp)
October retail sales +0.2% vs 0.1% expected; control group +0.6% — but part of it is inflation
Children's Place liquidating all stores; Grunt Style, Big Lots and IKEA closing more (secondary sources)
Retail CMBS delinquency +63bp to 7.21%; office highest at 12.33% (Trepp, October data)
Next week: short Thanksgiving week — Black Friday reads, Fed speakers, and whether the 10-year breaks 5%
friday.talking_point: Rates are still heading up, but October shoppers kept spending anyway — for well-located, grocery-anchored retail like Broad Street, that steady spending matters more to value than the cost of capital.
